title: Finite projective complex models for cohomology over an affine base
statement: Let A be a commutative ring and let f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A) be proper, flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let d\in\mathbf N and let F be a locally free O_X-module of constant rank d [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. For each q\ge0 there exists a cochain complex P of A-modules, indexed by the integers, with bounds a,b such that P^n=0 for n<a or b<n, each P^n finite and projective, and an A-linear isomorphism H^q(X,F)\cong H^q(P). The action of A on H^q(X,F) is restriction of scalars along A\cong\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}(A),O)\to\Gamma(X,O). Here H^q(P) is the kernel of the differential in degree q modulo the image of the preceding differential.

source.place: Lemma perfect-lemma-proper-flat-fp, Tag 0B91(2); Lemma perfect-lemma-perfect-affine, Tag 08EB; Cohomology of Sheaves, Tag 01F2

proof.text: Convert constant-rank local freeness to finite local freeness. On each pair of affine opens, sections of F are projective by [lem-pc-finite-flat-affine-sections-projective], hence flat over the source section ring. Flatness of f and Module.Flat.trans give relative flatness. The finite-presentation instance follows from finite local freeness. Use standard derived localizations; tensor pullback is additive because its adjunction makes it right exact. Apply the perfectness clause of [lem-pc-rf-perfect-base-change] to E = Rf_*(F[0]).

Apply [lem-sc-perfect-qcoherent] to E. Regard E as an object of D_QCoh and apply [lem-pc-perfect-affine-bounded-projective]. Unpack a bounded finite projective A-complex P and E isomorphic to Q(tilde(P)); combine the two termwise finiteness and projectivity predicates.

Apply the natural additive edge of [lem-pc-leray-degenerate-sections]. Its vanishing hypothesis is [lem-pc-affine-higher-direct-image-cohomology-vanishing]. For a section a of the base, specialize naturality to F.smulHom(f.appTop a). The source-library rightDerived_map_app_eq applied to module sections identifies the source endomorphism with scalar multiplication; higherDirectImage_map_smulHom and smulHom_app_top_apply identify the target endomorphism with multiplication by a. Thus the additive edge is linear over the base section ring. Bundle it as a module morphism and use its bijectivity to obtain an isomorphism.

Prove that tilde preserves kernels: by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel] the kernel of a morphism of associated sheaves is quasi-coherent. Its counit from [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] is invertible. Full faithfulness lifts that kernel fork to A-modules and reflects its limiting property. Since tilde is an additive left adjoint, it also preserves colimits, hence homology. Apply homology to the model isomorphism, then homologyFunctorFactors and mapHomologicalComplexHomologyIso, to identify H^q(E) with tilde(H^q(P)). The single-object cohomology comparison following [src-right-derived-functor-plus-compatibility] identifies H^q(E) with the ordinary right-derived module direct image.

Restrict the module Leray isomorphism along GammaSpecIso.inv. The scalar-restriction composition isomorphism identifies its source with the exact action specified in the statement. Evaluation followed by this restriction agrees with moduleSpecGammaFunctor: its extra terminal-object restriction is the identity on the ring, so the identity on the section carrier is a linear equivalence. Compose with sections of the derived homology comparisons and the inverse unit tilde.toTildeGammaNatIso from [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction]. This produces the required A-linear homology isomorphism. The argument has no nonemptiness or positive-rank assumption and works in degree zero and above the complex bounds.

mathlib_searches.results: Eight results concerned finite-presentation affine spaces, proper Proj, the valuative criterion, and flat scheme morphisms. None supplies a cohomology complex model.
Includes of_equiv and finitePresentation_of_projective; these address the algebraic consequence, not the geometric model.

from.place: Properness over a valuation ring makes global sections of an invertible module finitely presented; the finite-projective-complex model is its geometric input.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finiteProjectiveComplex_model_moduleCohomology
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    [IsProper f] [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (d : ℕ) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank d] (q : ℕ) :
    ∃ P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ,
      (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (P.X n)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite A (P.X n) ∧ Module.Projective A (P.X n)) ∧
      Nonempty (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom).obj
        ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace q).obj F)) ≅ P.homology (q : ℤ))
